product_scope: itpay is the single public Buyer CLI entry point, and $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation. It covers services, railway planning and booking, orders, authorized purchased content and refunds.
title: Order, Delivery, Customer Care And Refund Recovery
purpose: Read original orders and choose the current railway-aftercare or ordinary-refund path.
when_to_use: An order or Service Execution was interrupted after payment.
The buyer asks to request, track, or cancel a refund.
The human says money was charged but no result arrived, delivery failed, or asks what the refund policy means.
current_flow: Use itpay orders --json or itpay order <order_id> --json. Verified payment means do not pay again; retain the same order while fulfillment is pending or partial.

Railway: itpay aftercare list --order <order_id> --json returns original itinerary, leg/passenger targets and complete refund/change templates. Match the human’s explicit scope; ask only for missing scope. Explain manual handling before submitting.

Railway application acceptance, supplier return/change, platform refund and remaining-ticket validity are separate facts. Concrete change terms/revision/fees need actual consent. No automatic change payment or replacement ticket.

Ordinary service: use the order’s current refund action/template and policy. itpay refund get <refund_request_id> --json reads that original request; explicit watch is bounded, not an automatic repeat loop.

Respect platform delivery/access locks; a safe remaining-ticket read does not unlock content. Partial refund does not prove all tickets returned; a historic issued state does not prove present validity.
Read actual notification facts separately from ticket and money facts. Email/contact are chosen on the protected official page, not inferred from traveler/login phone.
